A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ColaVLA work, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. v1 ends after the references; v3 retains the main paper and adds supplementary Sections 6–9, which are included in this comparison.

before.justification: Tables 1–7 report original ColaVLA results on nuScenes and NeuroNCAP, including planning performance, inference latency and component ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds a planner-context ablation in Table 8 and qualitative closed-loop comparisons in Figure 5.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same two-pass cognitive reasoner, ego-adaptive router, meta-action bank and hierarchical parallel decoder. The supplement documents bank construction and training in greater detail, without establishing a replacement of the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use nuScenes, OmniDrive-nuScenes QA supervision and NeuroNCAP evaluation. The added closed-loop examples cover the static, frontal and side scenarios already evaluated in Table 2.

E2.justification: Table 8 adds a full-visual-token planner variant as a comparison against pruned-context ColaVLA. The named external baselines in Tables 1–3 and planner comparisons in Table 5 are unchanged. Figure 5 labels its comparator only 'Other Planner', so its identity cannot be established.

E3.justification: Section 6 adds a controlled full-versus-pruned planner-context experiment, keeping other components fixed. Section 7 reports three training stages, including separate meta-action-bank pretraining, whereas Section 4.1 describes QA pretraining followed by joint fine-tuning. v3 retains both accounts, leaving the actual schedule unresolved; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The existing four ablation studies remain. New Table 8 tests whether the planner benefits from attending only to selected critical tokens, and Figure 5 adds qualitative collision-avoidance cases under the existing NeuroNCAP scenarios.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Table 8 continues the existing practice of reporting point estimates and averages across prediction horizons.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their numerical results. New Table 8 reports full-context L2 errors of 14.8, 28.9 and 52.4 cm, averaging 32.0 cm, versus the already reported pruned-context values of 14.0, 27.1 and 50.2 cm, averaging 30.4 cm. Figure 5 adds qualitative outcomes; these additions do not demonstrate a version-to-version performance gain.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, including the latent representations and hybrid attention-mask definition, are retained. The supplement adds implementation descriptions without new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about latent reasoning, hierarchical parallel planning, efficiency, safety and state-of-the-art performance. The added project link and supplementary evidence do not redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: Section 9 newly explains why speed subclasses are restricted to frequent straight-driving paths while turning and lane-change speeds are pooled: avoiding severe class imbalance. This adds a substantive rationale and scope qualification for the meta-action representation; the broader safety and generalization interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 provides a brief architecture and optimizer description. v3 adds extensive architecture, preprocessing, training and meta-action-labeling details, including 16 H20 GPUs, batch size 32, 10 final-stage epochs, warmup, clipping, image dimensions, six planner scales and loss weights. Table 9 consolidates hyperparameters, and the abstract adds a project-repository link.

R1.justification: The reference list and related-work sections retain the same works and positioning. Section 9 adds a specific attribution that the meta-action categorization broadly follows Senna, which v1 cited only in its broader discussion of driving approaches.

P1.justification: The main narrative is essentially unchanged apart from the project-link sentence. v3 adds organized supplementary Sections 6–9 with expanded implementation explanations, without extensively rewriting or reorganizing the existing paper.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 8–9 and Figure 5. Table 3 moves from the left to the right column on page 7, with associated text and table reflow. Existing Figures 1–4 and the structures of Tables 1–7 are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's brief implementation account, v3 provides useful reproduction details and a focused validation of planner-context pruning. The gain is limited by the unreconciled two-stage versus three-stage training descriptions and Figure 5's unidentified comparator. The existing closed-loop discrepancy also remains: Section 4.2 reports a score of 3.16 and 42.5% collisions, whereas Table 2 reports 3.48 and 36.8%.
